Thanks again for the demo call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (what we covered)
- SDK setup: how the Redwood SDK bootstraps auth and token refresh for hosted vs private deployments.
- Auth options: API keys (short lived) vs mTLS for private; KMS/HSM for key management.
- Routing: per-route policies (latency vs cost) and fallback model variants.
- Tool/function calling: recommended tool definitions (schema-driven JSON), synchronous vs async execution, parallel enrichment patterns.
- Embeddings + reranker: using an embeddings index for retrieval, then lightweight reranker to improve precision.
- Error handling: idempotency keys, retries with backoff, graceful degradation (fallback to cached responses or simpler model).

Internal notes / suggested agenda for the technical deep-dive with FinApps:

1) Quick 10m intro (teams + objectives)
2) Auth & SDK: show SDK init code for hosted vs private, token rotation, and example mTLS config for private cloud.
3) Tool schemas: recommend explicit JSON tool definitions with typed params, examples, and validator step inside the runtime. Emphasize schema-first to avoid ambiguous inputs.
4) Execution model:
   - Short-running tools: sync call + return structured JSON to LLM to continue.
   - Long-running jobs (batch/calculator): async pattern — return job id to LLM, surface polling or webhook callback to complete flow.
   - Parallel enrichment pattern: fire off search + metadata fetch in parallel, assemble results, then run a reranker.
5) Reranker guidance:
   - Candidate pool: typically 50–200 for p95 200–400ms reranking depending on model size; can reduce by two-stage candidate filtering.
   - Cost tradeoff: use small lightweight cross-encoder for rerank to save cost; measure MRR/precision on heldout queries.
6) Error handling & fallbacks:
   - Idempotency keys for tool calls, retries with exponential backoff, circuit breaker for downstreams.
   - Fallback to cached answer or to a safe, generic response template when a critical tool fails.

Suggested times from FinApps (Tue/Wed mornings PST) — I'll propose Tue 06/16 9:30am or Wed 06/17 10:00am.

Also attaching a small example tool schema I put together (example-tool-schema.json) and a one-pager on async patterns.

Alex — thanks for the answers. Wed 06/17 at 10:00am PT works for us; sending a calendar invite now.

To your question on reranker latency/cost: Lauren's note outlines our starting prescriptive defaults (50–200 candidates, two-stage filtering). For your 800ms p95 target we recommend:
- Use a 2-stage retrieval: sparse or ANN search to get ~200 candidates, then a lightweight reranker (small cross-encoder) to cut to the top 10 before generation.
- Benchmark: on x86/GPU optimized runtime expect ~150–350ms extra for reranking depending on model; we can run a short perf test in your environment during the PoC.
